If you’re frustrated with mandatory classes, that’s understandable—but there are more constructive ways to handle it than walking out in a huff. Learning to engage (even passively) is a skill that will help you in jobs, relationships, and other situations where you might not agree with the rules. --- ### **TL;DR** You were wrong to walk out because: - It was disrespectful to the instructor and the class’s purpose. - It violated school rules and could have consequences. - There were better ways to handle your discomfort (e.g., staying quietly or leaving after class). A better response would have been to stay engaged (even minimally) or leave calmly. Now, own up to it, follow the school’s process, and use this as a lesson in handling mandatory but unpleasant tasks.
